simple.meaning: קִיתָרֹס (qîythârôç) is a Hebrew word meaning “a lyre.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קִיתָרֹס (H7030) appears 8 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 3:5, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קִיתָרֹס (H7030) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קִיתָרֹס (H7030) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: קִיתָרֹס (qîythârôç) / H7030 is traced through Daniel 3:5, Daniel 3:7, Daniel 3:10, Daniel 3:15 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: that whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, you fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king has set up.

definitions.full: H7030. qitharos קיתרס Kt, קַתְרֹס Qr, noun [masculine] lyre, zither (also ᵑ7 ; loan-word from Greek κίθαρις Krauss i. 193: ii. 573 ); — Dan 3:5 , 7 , 10 , 15 ; Kmp קִיתָרִם . קָל see קול .
